questions: Q1: What is the current hlx inspect subcommand pattern and how does it extend to netsuite?
Q2: What new top-level command is needed for hlx run and what infrastructure supports it?
Q3: How does the HTTP client handle basePath and auth for different endpoint types?
Q4: Does the CLI need an --env flag or is environment purely token-bounded?

answers.answer: The inspect subcommand router (src/inspect/index.ts:41-128) uses a switch on args[0] with existing cases: repos, db, logs, api. Each handler is 10-14 lines following the pattern: resolveRepo -> hxFetch POST/GET -> console.log JSON. Adding 'netsuite' requires one new case in the switch and one new handler file (src/inspect/netsuite.ts). The handler follows src/inspect/db.ts exactly: resolveRepo -> hxFetch POST /{repoId}/netsuite with { query } body. The --query-file flag handling (lines 70-88) is in the router and extends naturally to netsuite. Help text at lines 9-31 needs updating.
evidence: src/inspect/index.ts:42-128 — switch on args[0] with cases: repos, db, logs, api, default
src/inspect/db.ts:1-12 — Full handler: import config/http/resolve-repo, resolveRepo, hxFetch POST /{repoId}/database, console.log JSON
src/inspect/index.ts:70-88 — --query-file flag reading with readFileSync, error handling, empty check
src/inspect/index.ts:9-31 — help text with usage examples for all subcommands

answers.answer: No 'run' case exists in the main dispatcher (src/index.ts:81-156 — verified by exhaustive switch inspection). A new top-level case is needed at src/index.ts alongside inspect/comments/preview/etc. It follows the configOrHelp pattern (lines 26-35). A new module src/run/index.ts is needed (src/run/ directory does not exist). The handler will: parse --repo, --script-file or inline code, hxFetch POST with body { code, modules? }, and print JSON result.
evidence: src/index.ts:82-155 — All existing cases: login, token, inspect, comments, preview, library, org, tickets, goals, skill, update, --version, --help, default — NO 'run' case
ls src/run/ — directory does not exist
src/index.ts:26-35 — configOrHelp pattern: isHelpRequested check -> loadConfig or requireConfig

answers.answer: hxFetch (src/lib/http.ts:37-130) defaults to basePath='/api/inspect' (line 43) but accepts basePath override via options parameter. Auth is dual-mode: hxi_ tokens use X-API-Key header, others use Authorization: Bearer (lines 52-61). For hlx inspect netsuite, the default basePath works if the server endpoint is POST /api/inspect/{repoId}/netsuite. For hlx run, the basePath may need override to '/api' if the server route is POST /api/run/{repoId}. The goals command already demonstrates basePath override.
evidence: src/lib/http.ts:52-61 — dual-mode auth: hxi_ -> X-API-Key; else -> Authorization: Bearer
src/lib/http.ts:37-41 — hxFetch signature with basePath in options

answers.answer: Environment is token-bounded (nsEnv claim set at token issuance time based on workflow step). The CLI does not need an --env flag for sandbox agents — the token already encodes the allowed environment. For human users with hxi_ API keys, an --env flag may be useful but is a future consideration. The initial implementation should not add an --env flag.
evidence: session.ts:102-112 — Token claims set at issuance; no CLI-side env selection in current inspection flow
src/lib/config.ts:42-45 — HELIX_INSPECT_TOKEN env var used by sandbox agents; token carries all claims
Continuation context — 'the CLI may select env only within what the token authorizes; per-step default routing stays'

statement: The helix-cli needs two new commands matching the two-surface governance model: (1) 'hlx inspect netsuite' as a new case in the inspect router following the established db/logs/api handler pattern (~12 lines per handler), and (2) 'hlx run' as a new top-level command in the main dispatcher. Both use the existing hxFetch HTTP client with dual-mode auth and retry logic. No new dependencies needed (zero runtime deps). Environment routing is token-bounded — no --env flag required for sandbox agents. The implementation is low-risk: small additions following verified patterns with no modifications to existing handlers.
